Projects are saved automatically in this browser. To keep and share safely: Save project as file.
Tracery computes with OpenCascade (LGPL-2.1) via replicad (MIT) and renders 3D with three.js (MIT).

menu.main.aboutP1: Tracery is a free, parametric CAD in the browser – no account required, with an exact geometry kernel and technical drawings.
menu.main.aboutP2: The name: “Tracery” refers to the delicate, precisely constructed stone ribs in Gothic windows. That is how your parts should turn out.
menu.main.aboutP3: Powered by the OpenCascade CAD kernel (LGPL-2.1) via replicad (MIT). 3D rendering uses three.js (MIT), PDF output uses jsPDF (MIT).
menu.main.aboutP4: Your projects stay in your browser. The AI assistant uses your Claude account.

panel.sweep.boundInfo: P{n} is attached to “{name}” and follows it
panel.sweep.routeHint: The pipe runs through points in 3D space – great for cable channels, tubes and brackets bending in all directions. Set Wall to make it hollow.
panel.sweep.wrapHint: The profile sweeps along the wrapped 3D curve. Use Body above to join or cut it directly with the cylinder.
panel.sweep.pathHint: The profile sweeps along the path – great for pipes, cable channels, brackets and rails. Set Wall to make it hollow.
panel.loft.tipHint: Extend to tip converges the body past the last profile to a point – e.g. for a nose cone or smooth taper. You can fillet edges afterwards as usual.
panel.loft.pathAngleWarn: The centerline meets {which} at a steep angle ({angs}). The body may become thin or twisted – keep it roughly perpendicular to the profiles.
panel.loft.pathActiveHint: The loft follows the centerline. Tip and “Ruled faces” are disabled in this mode.
panel.loft.pathIdleHint: Without a centerline, the loft takes the shortest path. Add a Centerline to bend it – e.g. a curved pipe or sculpted housing.
panel.loft.needTwoPath: A centerline requires at least two profiles.
panel.loft.railActiveHint: Between profiles, the loft follows the guide curve – e.g. a handle or housing that bulges in the middle. The profiles themselves stay the same.
panel.loft.railIdleHint: A Guide curve defines the side silhouette: the loft widens or narrows between profiles without needing extra profile sketches.
panel.loft.railBlockedPath: Cannot use a guide curve together with a centerline – pick “No centerline” first.
panel.loft.needTwoRail: A guide curve requires at least two profiles.
panel.loft.rail2ActiveHint: The loft follows both guide curves – each controls the width along its direction.
panel.loft.rail2IdleHint: The first guide curve shapes the width in one direction. A second curve perpendicular to it shapes the other – defining a hull from the side and top.
panel.loft.pathBlockedRail: Cannot use a centerline together with a guide curve – pick “No guide curve” first.

left.fs.title: First Steps
left.fs.bodyHow: Click “Body” at the top and pick a box or cylinder – or drag it onto the workplane.
left.fs.sizeHow: Click the body and drag an arrow – or type a new number on the right under “Dimensions”.
left.fs.holeHow: Add a cylinder, slide it into the first body and click “Make hole” in the top bar.
left.fs.saveHow: Click “Export” at the top. STL is the file format for 3D printers.
left.fs.done: Well done – you know the basics! See the introduction on the home screen for more.

left.par.badName: Names may only contain letters, digits and _ and must not start with a digit.
left.par.tablesHintHtml: Small two-column lookup tables (key and value) – usable in formulas like tabelle(Screw; M5).
left.par.badTableName: Table names may only contain letters, digits and _ and must not start with a digit.
left.par.needKey: Please enter a key for the row.
left.par.needVal: Please enter a number or formula.

left.par.tblExists: A table with this name already exists.

left.par.formulaIntroHtml: Supported: + − * / ^, comparisons < > <= >= == !=, parentheses, pi and functions if(cond; then; else) / wenn, round(x; digits) / runden, ceil, floor, tabelle(name; key), min, max, abs, sqrt, sin, cos, tan (angles in degrees). Separate multiple arguments with ; – e.g. max(a; b). Both dot and comma decimals work.
left.par.formulaCopyFail: Copy failed – simply highlight and copy the formula.
left.par.formulaAddedDemo: {n} dimensions created – you can now use these formulas anywhere.
sk.toolTip.line: Draw polyline – close at start point

sk.toolTip.tpl: Ready-made outlines: pin headers, vent grilles, chips (QFP, QFN, BGA, SOIC, DIP), USB-C cutouts, mounting holes
sk.toolTip.text: Text as outline – for embossing or cutting
sk.toolTip.spline: Spline: smooth curve through points – Enter finishes
sk.toolTip.corner: Fillet or chamfer corner between two lines – works on rectangles and polygons too
sk.toolTip.extend: Extend line to the next edge
sk.toolTip.splitl: Split line or arc at a point into two segments
sk.toolTip.offset: Parallel copy at distance – stays linked by constraint
sk.toolTip.wall: Turn an open line into a wall with thickness – e.g. ribs and webs
sk.toolTip.project: Project an edge or Shift + click a whole flat face (with optional offset) into the sketch
sk.toolTip.mirror: Mirror across a line – adds symmetry constraints
sk.toolTip.patrect: Repeat entities in rows and columns
sk.toolTip.xmove: Move entities by an exact distance or rotate around a point – also as copy
sk.toolTip.dim: Set dimension – also as formula like width/2

sk.hint.select: Click an entity or drag a box in empty space (left→right: fully inside · right→left: touching · Shift adds). Endpoints can be dragged. Del deletes, H moves.
sk.hint.line: Click sets points (snaps to 15° steps and round lengths · hold Shift for free). A switches between line and tangent arc. Type a number for exact length. Close at start or press Enter to finish.
sk.hint.rect: Click first corner, then opposite corner. Or type numbers: width Tab height.
sk.hint.circle: Click center, then size. Or type diameter.
sk.hint.bg: Load a photo or drawing as reference. Click Set scale, pick two points with a known distance – then the size matches. Drag to move the image.
sk.hint.bgcal: Click the first point on the image, then the second. Then type the real distance.
sk.hint.splitl: Click on a line or arc – it splits into two connected pieces at that point. Snaps to midpoints and intersections.
sk.hint.extend: Click near the end of a line – it extends up to the next line, arc or circle and locks onto it.
sk.hint.project: Click an edge to project it linked into the sketch. Shift + click a flat face to project all boundary edges (outer and holes) at once – with Offset on the right (+ outward / − inward). Plain click on a face projects the section.
sk.hint.wall: Set thickness on the right, then click an open line, arc or spline – turns into a closed wall ready to extrude. The original line stays as a construction centerline.
sk.hint.point: Click places a point. Points do not form faces, but serve as references for dimensions and constraints. On a body face, standalone points become holes on Done.
sk.hint.tpl: Choose template and sizes on the right, then click in the viewport – the click sets the center. Snaps to origin and centers.
sk.hint.text: Set text, height and font on the right, then click in the viewport. The click sets the start of the baseline (or center if aligned “Center”).
sk.hint.ellipse: Click center, then end of first axis (sets length and rotation), then width. Or type width Tab height.
sk.hint.arc: Click start point, end point, then bulge.
sk.hint.slot: Click first and second centers, then width.
sk.hint.poly: Click center, then size. Set number of sides on the right.
sk.hint.spline: Click to place points along the curve. Close at first point, double-click last point or press Enter to finish.
sk.hint.corner: Hover over a corner where two lines meet – rectangles and polygons work too. Click rounds it with the radius on the right. Switch to chamfer on the right.
sk.hint.trim: Hover over a segment between two intersections – it glows red. Click trims it away, or hold mouse button to drag-trim.
sk.hint.offset: Click a line, circle or shape. On the right you can choose Count, Both sides and Corners (sharp/round). Move mouse to one side and click – or type distance and press Enter.
sk.hint.mirror: First click the mirror line (any line, including construction lines), then click the entities to mirror. Press Enter to mirror all.
sk.hint.patrect: Click the entities to repeat. Set count and spacing on the right, then press Enter.
sk.hint.patcirc: Click the entities to repeat in a circle. Set count, angle and center on the right, then press Enter.
sk.hint.xmove: Click the entities to move or rotate. Set distance or angle on the right, then press Enter. With “As copy” the original stays.
sk.hint.dim: Click a line, rectangle side, circle or arc and type the dimension – even a formula like width/2. For a distance click two points (or point and line), for an angle click two lines.
sk.chint.horizontal: Click a line – or two points to align horizontally.
sk.chint.vertical: Click a line – or two points to align vertically.
sk.chint.parallel: Click two lines to make parallel.
sk.chint.perpendicular: Click two lines to form a right angle.
sk.chint.collinear: Click two lines to lie on the same infinite line – like two segments of a broken edge.
sk.chint.tangent: Click a line and a circle/arc – or two circles that should touch smoothly.
sk.chint.equal: Click two lines (equal length) or two circles (equal radius).
sk.chint.symmetric: Click two points or circles, then the mirror line.
sk.chint.coincident: Click two points – or a point and the line or circle it should lie on.
sk.chint.fix: Click an entity or point to lock it in place.
sk.chint.midpoint: Click a point (or circle), then the line whose midpoint it should lie on.
sk.chint.concentric: Click two circles, arcs or ellipses – they share the same center.
sk.chint.project: Click a dashed face edge – it becomes a solid line in your sketch.
sk.chint.xform: The copy follows its original: when the original changes, the copy updates. You can edit spacing or angle here.
sk.chint.offset: The copy stays at a fixed distance from the original. When the original changes, the copy follows. You can edit the distance here.
sk.start.where: Where would you like to draw?
sk.start.tip: Tip: Click a flat face on a body and choose “Sketch here” to draw directly on it.
sk.start.pick3pHint: Plane through 3 points: Click point {n} of 3 on a body – corners and edge midpoints snap. Esc cancels.
sk.start.pickMidClick: Click a flat face on a body.
sk.start.pickMidFail: The two faces are not parallel – a midplane only works between parallel faces.
sk.start.pick3pFail: Those three points are collinear – they do not define a plane.
sk.start.pickMidOk: Sketch on the midplane – centered between both faces.
sk.start.pick3pOk: Sketch on the plane through the three points.

sk.panel.patPathHint: Curve for the pattern – copies follow it from start to end. The dot marks the original: it starts from the closer end of the curve. A circle or closed loop distributes copies all around.
sk.panel.loftRailHint: Guide curve for loft – defines the side profile: between cross-sections, the loft expands or narrows to touch this curve. The profiles themselves stay unchanged. It should span from the first to the last profile.
sk.panel.loftRail2Hint: Second guide curve – perpendicular to the first, controlling width in the other direction (e.g. top view when the first defines the side). The loft follows both while keeping the profiles intact.
sk.panel.loftPathHint: Centerline for loft – profiles stay in place (shown by thin guide edges) while the loft bends along this curve. It should run from the first profile through all others to the last. Drag curve points or draw a new line, arc or spline.
sk.panel.stepRevHint: Choose the axis of revolution. Click regions in the viewport to select or deselect them.
sk.panel.stepExtHint: Drag the arrow in the viewport or type the height. Click regions to select or deselect them.
sk.panel.freeInfo: {dof} missing {dofWord} ({pts} movable {ptsWord}). Click an orange dot to wiggle it.
sk.panel.confIntro: Involved constraints and dimensions – click to highlight or remove one:
sk.panel.conBadVal: This value conflicts with the other constraints.

sk.step.pickFaceClick: Click a face in the viewport …

sk.step.sweepDesc: Sweeps a Ø 6 mm pipe along the open path. Profile, size and wall can be adjusted on the right afterwards.
sk.step.extPickHint: Click the target face or a datum plane in the 3D view.
sk.step.revPickHint: Pick target face: Click a flat body face or a datum plane.

sk.step.resJoin: Will join the body you sketched on.

draw.dimHint.lin: Dimension: Click two points, then place the dimension line. Clicking a circle dimensions its diameter. Esc exits.
draw.dimHint.chain: Chain dimension: Click start point, second point and dimension line, then click additional points along the chain. Enter finishes the chain, Esc exits.
draw.dimHint.base: Baseline dimension: Click reference edge or point, first target and dimension line, then click further targets. Enter finishes, Esc exits.
draw.dimHint.ang: Angular dimension: Click two angled edges, then place the angle arc. Esc exits.
draw.dimHint.rad: Radius: Click a fillet or circular arc to display R. Esc exits.
draw.dimHint.dia: Diameter: Click a hole or circle to display Ø. Esc exits.
draw.dimHint.chamfer: Chamfer: Click a chamfered edge to display distance × angle. Esc exits.
draw.hint.detail: Detail view: Click center of circle inside a view, drag circle, then place the detail view on the sheet. Esc exits.
draw.hint.section: Section view: Drag section line A–A through a view or click two points (Shift = horizontal/vertical, Alt = free). Esc exits.
draw.hint.note: Leader note: Click an edge (arrow) or face (dot), then choose where to place the text. Esc exits.
draw.sheetMinToast: At least one sheet must remain.
draw.autoDimsToast: Overall dimensions and holes have been dimensioned.
draw.tb.title: Title
draw.png.hint: Height adapts automatically to sheet aspect ratio. Recommended: 2400 px for documents or 300 DPI for printing.
draw.panel.tolOutOfRange: {code}: Nominal size is outside the ISO 286 table (0–500 mm).
draw.panel.helpHintHtml: Views follow First-angle projection: top view below front view, left side view to its right (drag views to reposition). Select a view on the sheet or in the list to adjust scale, edges or shading. Use Section View (S) to cut a line A–A, Detail View (Z) to enlarge a region at its own scale, and Leader Note (N) to attach notes to edges or faces. Click any dimension to add tolerances (±, deviations, limits) or ISO 286 fits (H7, g6 …) – or select a dimension, section, detail, note or centerline and press Del to remove or hide it.
dlg.settings.title: Settings
dlg.settings.levelHint: Simple hides Measure, Notes, View, Drawing and Pro tools. You can still reach them via “More”.
dlg.settings.decHint: Applies to labels, dimensions, measurements and panels. Stored values and compute precision always remain exact.
dlg.settings.unitHint: Applies to all displays, dimensions and inputs without explicit units in this project.
dlg.settings.qualityHint: How smooth curves look on screen. Actual geometry is always exact.
dlg.settings.mTracery: Tracery – left orbits, right pans, wheel zooms
dlg.settings.mOnshape: Like Onshape – right orbits, middle pans
dlg.settings.mSolidworks: Like SolidWorks – middle orbits, right pans
dlg.settings.mFusion: Like Fusion – middle pans, Shift + middle orbits
dlg.settings.mBlender: Like Blender – middle orbits, Shift + middle pans
dlg.settings.mouseHint: In all presets except Tracery, left-dragging in empty space draws a selection box. The scroll wheel always zooms.
dlg.settings.adaptiveHint: Parts viewed up close are refined automatically. When orbiting large models, rendering briefly coarsens to stay smooth.
dlg.settings.multiWorkerHint: Distributes independent bodies across up to {n} compute workers simultaneously (matching your {cores} CPU cores). Speeds up large models.
dlg.settings.multiWorkerSingleHint: Your device reports only 1 CPU core – Tracery will run with a single compute worker.
dlg.settings.levelSimpleToast: Simple: fewer, larger buttons, everything explained.
dlg.settings.levelProToast: Pro: all tools and keyboard shortcuts.
dlg.export.nothing: Nothing to export yet. Add a body first.
dlg.export.intro: Files are bundled into a ZIP archive.
dlg.export.stepSub: Exact geometry with part names, colors and groups – for Fusion, FreeCAD, SolidWorks and manufacturers
dlg.export.igesSub: Exact surfaces and solids – for older CAD and CAM software
dlg.export.brepSub: Native OpenCascade format – lossless for FreeCAD and Tracery
dlg.export.objSub: Triangle mesh with colors – for Blender, rendering and many 3D apps
dlg.export.glbSub: 3D file with material appearance and part names – for web, Blender and previews
dlg.export.stlSub: Triangle mesh, e.g. for rendering or 3D printing
dlg.export.mfSub: Triangle mesh with colors and units
dlg.export.onlySelSub: Everything else is excluded – holes and features on the selected parts are included
dlg.export.holeCompHint: Enlarges round internal holes only in 3D print files (STL/3MF) – the model and STEP remain exact.
dlg.export.each: Each body as separate file (STL, 3MF, OBJ, GLB)
dlg.export.eachSub: Adds a folder with one file per body named after the part – handy for slicers
dlg.export.dxfSub: Top-down 1:1 outline, one file per plate – thickness is included in the filename
